title: Plants
description: Plants have parts like roots, stems, leaves, and flowers. They make new plants through seeds. Flowering plants have life cycles from seed to flower.

exercises.question: What do ROOTS do for a plant?
choices: absorb water and hold the plant in soil
exercises.exp: Roots anchor the plant in the ground and soak up water and nutrients from the soil.

exercises.question: What is the main job of LEAVES?
exercises.exp: Leaves capture sunlight and use it along with water and CO₂ to make food — this is photosynthesis!

exercises.question: What do FLOWERS do for a plant?
exercises.exp: Flowers attract bees, butterflies, and birds to help with pollination so the plant can make seeds.

exercises.question: Which part of a plant carries water from the roots to the leaves?
exercises.exp: The stem is like a straw — it carries water and nutrients from the roots to the rest of the plant.

exercises.question: Is a tomato a fruit or a vegetable?
choices: it is a vegetable because it is savoury
it is a fruit because it contains seeds
exercises.exp: Scientifically, a tomato is a FRUIT — any part of a plant that contains seeds is a fruit!

exercises.question: What is the correct order of a flowering plant's life cycle?
exercises.exp: Seeds grow into seedlings, then adult plants, then they flower and make new seeds!

exercises.question: How do DANDELION seeds travel to new places?
choices: they are carried by the wind
exercises.exp: Dandelion seeds have feathery tufts that catch the wind and carry them far away!

exercises.question: A maple tree makes MAPLE KEYS (helicopter seeds). How do they travel?
choices: they spin in the wind and blow away
exercises.exp: Maple keys spin like helicopter blades in the wind, carrying seeds to new spots.

exercises.question: Which plant part stores the most FOOD?
exercises.exp: Root vegetables like carrots, beets, and potatoes store lots of food energy for the plant.

exercises.question: What happens FIRST when a seed germinates?
choices: a tiny root breaks through the seed coat
exercises.exp: When a seed germinates, the tiny root pushes down first to find water, then the shoot grows up!

exercises.question: Which is NOT a plant part?
exercises.exp: Gills are part of fish — not plants! Plants have roots, stems, leaves, and flowers.

exercises.question: What do plants need to make their own food?
exercises.exp: Plants use sunlight + water + CO₂ to make sugar (food) through photosynthesis. Amazing!

exercises.question: What gas do plants TAKE IN during photosynthesis?
exercises.exp: Plants absorb carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the air through tiny pores in their leaves called stomata.

exercises.question: Why do plants NEED water?
choices: for photosynthesis, transporting nutrients, and keeping cells firm
water has no function in plants
exercises.exp: Water is essential for photosynthesis, carrying dissolved minerals, and keeping plant cells firm (turgid) so they don't wilt.

exercises.question: What is POLLINATION?
choices: when pollen is transferred from one flower to another, allowing seed formation
when seeds are dispersed by wind
when a plant loses its leaves
exercises.exp: Pollination moves pollen (often with help from bees, butterflies, or wind) from flower to flower, enabling seeds to form.

exercises.question: Which plant part is underground and absorbs water?
exercises.exp: Roots grow underground, anchoring the plant and absorbing water and nutrients dissolved in the soil.

exercises.question: A PINE TREE makes CONES instead of flowers. How does it make seeds?
choices: it cannot make seeds — only flowering plants can
seeds form inside the cones after pollination by wind
it uses insects to pollinate its cones
exercises.exp: Pine trees are conifers — they make seeds in cones, not flowers! Wind blows pollen from male cones to female cones.

exercises.question: Why do plants produce SWEET NECTAR in their flowers?
choices: to make the flower smell nice
to attract pollinators like bees and butterflies who help with pollination
exercises.exp: Nectar is a sweet reward that attracts pollinators — they drink the nectar and accidentally carry pollen between flowers!

exercises.question: A VENUS FLYTRAP catches and digests insects. Why does it need insects?
choices: it grows in soil poor in nutrients — insects provide extra nitrogen it cannot get from soil
it is an animal, not a plant
insects provide water to the plant
exercises.exp: Venus flytraps live in nutrient-poor boggy soil. They trap insects to get nitrogen — a nutrient they cannot get from the soil!

exercises.question: What happens if a plant does NOT get enough SUNLIGHT?
choices: it becomes pale, weak, and may die — cannot make enough food
exercises.exp: Without sunlight, plants cannot photosynthesize — they run out of energy, turn yellow and weak, and eventually die.

exercises.question: Seeds can travel by WATER. Which plant's seeds float and travel across oceans?
choices: a coconut palm — coconuts float and drift to new shores
exercises.exp: Coconuts are perfectly adapted for ocean travel — their waterproof outer husk helps them float and stay viable for months!

exercises.question: ANNUAL plants complete their life cycle in ONE year. What happens to them after they set seeds?
choices: they keep growing for many more years
they die — but their seeds grow into new plants next year
exercises.exp: Annual plants live for one growing season — they grow, flower, make seeds, then die. The seeds start the cycle again!

exercises.question: Which part of a plant makes SEEDS?
exercises.exp: After a flower is pollinated, its ovary develops into fruit containing seeds — the flower is the plant's reproductive organ.

exercises.question: Why do plants need SOIL?
choices: soil gives plants their green colour
soil provides minerals, water, and anchorage for roots
plants do not need soil — they only need light
soil prevents plants from growing too tall
exercises.exp: Soil provides essential minerals (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium) dissolved in water that roots absorb, plus anchorage.

exercises.question: What type of plant is a FERN?
choices: a non-flowering plant that reproduces by spores instead of seeds
exercises.exp: Ferns are ancient non-flowering plants — they reproduce using tiny spores found in brown dots on the underside of their fronds.

exercises.question: A gardener wants plants to grow BIGGER FASTER. What should she add to the soil?
choices: fertiliser containing nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium
exercises.exp: Fertiliser provides key nutrients plants need to grow — nitrogen for leaves, phosphorus for roots and flowers, potassium for health!

exercises.question: Which is TRUE about EVERGREEN trees?
choices: they lose all their leaves in autumn
they keep their leaves (usually needles) all year round
they only grow near the equator
exercises.exp: Evergreen trees like pines, spruces, and firs keep their needle-like leaves through winter — staying green all year!

exercises.question: What is the difference between a FRUIT and a VEGETABLE scientifically?
choices: fruits are sweet and vegetables are savoury
a fruit contains seeds and develops from a flower; a vegetable is any other edible plant part
fruits grow on trees and vegetables grow underground
exercises.exp: Scientifically, a fruit is the seed-bearing part from a flower. Vegetables are other plant parts — roots, stems, or leaves.

exercises.question: Mosses grow on DAMP ROCKS and TREES. They have no roots — how do they absorb water?
choices: they cannot absorb water at all
they absorb water directly through their tiny leaf-like structures from rain and dew
they absorb water from the air only
exercises.exp: Mosses have no true roots — they absorb water directly through their surface. That is why they need damp environments!

exercises.question: A plant BENDS TOWARD LIGHT. This behaviour is called ___.
exercises.exp: Phototropism is a plant's growth response to light — shoots grow toward light to maximise photosynthesis!

exercises.question: Which plant structure produces OXYGEN as a by-product of photosynthesis?
exercises.exp: Leaves are the photosynthesis powerhouses — they take in CO₂ and release oxygen (O₂) as a by-product. Every breath you take thanks a leaf!

exercises.question: What are the FOUR main parts of a plant?
exercises.exp: The four main parts of a plant are roots (absorb water), stem (supports, transports), leaves (photosynthesis), and flowers (reproduction)!

exercises.question: What do ROOTS do for a plant? (Choose the BEST answer)
choices: only hold the plant in the ground
absorb water and minerals from the soil AND anchor the plant in the ground
exercises.exp: Roots anchor the plant AND absorb water and minerals. Some roots (like carrots) also store food!

exercises.question: Leaves are GREEN because they contain ___.
choices: chlorophyll — the green pigment that captures light for photosynthesis
exercises.exp: Chlorophyll is the green pigment inside leaf cells. It captures light energy — the first step in making food through photosynthesis.

exercises.question: The process by which water moves UP through a plant from roots to leaves is called ___.
exercises.exp: Water travels up through tiny tube-like cells (xylem) by capillary action. It evaporates from leaves — this pull draws more water up!

exercises.question: A plant in a dark cupboard will eventually ___.
choices: die because it cannot photosynthesize without light
exercises.exp: Without light, a plant cannot photosynthesize and make food — it uses up stored energy and eventually dies.

exercises.question: Flowers attract bees with colour and sweet nectar. Bees carry POLLEN from flower to flower. This helps plants ___.
choices: reproduce — pollen fertilises the eggs in other flowers to make seeds
exercises.exp: Pollination by bees (and other insects, birds, wind) carries pollen to fertilise flowers — making fruits and seeds for new plants!

exercises.question: What is GERMINATION?
choices: a leaf falling from a tree
when a seed begins to sprout and grow into a new plant
roots growing deeper in the ground
exercises.exp: Germination is when a seed sprouts — given water, warmth, and oxygen, the seed swells and a tiny shoot and root emerge!

exercises.question: Which is NOT needed for a seed to germinate?
choices: light (NOT essential for germination — seeds can germinate in the dark!)
exercises.exp: Seeds do NOT need light to germinate — they need water, warmth, and oxygen. Light becomes important once the seedling appears!

exercises.question: EVERGREEN trees ___.
choices: lose all their leaves in autumn
keep their leaves all year round
exercises.exp: Evergreen trees (like pine and spruce) keep their leaves (usually needles) throughout the year — they stay green all year!

exercises.question: DECIDUOUS trees drop their leaves in autumn because ___.
choices: they conserve water and energy during cold winter months when light is limited
exercises.exp: Deciduous trees shed leaves to reduce water loss and save energy during winter — a brilliant survival adaptation!

exercises.question: What is the role of POLLEN in plant reproduction?
choices: it provides food for the plant
it is the male reproductive cell that fertilises the egg in a flower to make a seed
exercises.exp: Pollen contains the plant's male sex cells. When pollen fertilises the egg in a flower's ovary, a seed is formed — new life begins!

exercises.question: How do DANDELION seeds travel to new places?
choices: they float on the wind using fluffy parachutes attached to each seed
exercises.exp: Dandelion seeds have feathery 'parachutes' — the slightest breeze carries them far and wide. Wind dispersal at its best!

exercises.question: A CACTUS stores water in its thick stem and has spines instead of leaves. These are ___.
choices: adaptations for surviving in hot, dry deserts with little water
exercises.exp: Cacti are brilliantly adapted to desert life — thick stems store water, waxy coating reduces water loss, spines deter animals!

exercises.question: Which part of the plant produces SEEDS?
exercises.exp: After a flower is pollinated, the ovary develops into a fruit containing seeds — the next generation of plants!

exercises.question: What is the function of the STEM?
choices: only to hold the plant upright
to transport water and nutrients between roots and leaves AND support the plant
exercises.exp: The stem is the plant's highway — it transports water (up, via xylem) and sugars (down, via phloem) AND holds the plant upright.

exercises.question: Plants that grow in the RAINFOREST have large, broad leaves because ___.
choices: they need to collect lots of rain
large leaves capture more of the limited sunlight that filters through the dense canopy above
exercises.exp: In a rainforest, tall trees shade the floor. Plants near the ground have large leaves to capture every bit of light available!

exercises.question: VENUS FLYTRAP is a plant that traps and digests insects. Why does it eat insects?
choices: it lives in poor soils lacking nutrients — insects provide extra nitrogen and minerals
exercises.exp: Venus flytraps grow in nutrient-poor wetland soils. By trapping insects, they get the nitrogen and minerals the soil cannot provide!

exercises.question: What process do plants use to RELEASE WATER VAPOUR through their leaves?
exercises.exp: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaf surfaces. On a hot day, a large tree can transpire hundreds of litres of water!

exercises.question: Which is the correct order of a plant's life cycle?
choices: seed → germination → seedling → adult plant → flower → seed
exercises.exp: Seed → germinates → seedling grows → adult plant → flowers → pollination → new seeds. The cycle continues!

exercises.question: SEAWEED is a plant-like organism that lives in the ocean. It does NOT have roots because ___.
choices: it gets too cold in water for roots
it absorbs water and nutrients directly through its whole body — it is submerged in nutrient-rich seawater
it moves around too much for roots
roots only work in soil, not saltwater
exercises.exp: Seaweed is bathed in nutrient-rich seawater — it absorbs what it needs through its surface. No need for roots to seek water!
